content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To address a letter to a government official, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Draft the formal salutation (5 minutes)
Step 2. Research the official's current subcommittee assignments (45 minutes)
Step 3. Draft the specific policy recommendation (1 hour)
Step 4. Print the final letter on high-quality bond paper (2 minutes)
Step 5. Proofread for grammatical errors (15 minutes)
Step 6. Check the spelling of the official's name (5 minutes)
Step 7. Locate the official's office suite number (10 minutes)
Step 8. Place the letter into the envelope (30 seconds)
Step 9. Verify the ZIP code for the capital district (5 minutes)
Step 10. Identify the correct government department (20 minutes)
Step 11. Outline the main concerns of the letter (30 minutes)
Step 12. Determine the correct honorific to use (e.g., The Honorable) (10 minutes)
Step 13. Brainstorm the core message of the correspondence (1 hour)
Step 14. Gather your personal contact information (5 minutes)
Step 15. Write the introductory paragraph (20 minutes)
Step 16. Apply a decorative wax seal (3 minutes)
Step 17. Sign the letter with a blue ink pen (1 minute)
Step 18. Review the letter for tone and clarity (20 minutes)
Step 19. Format the recipient's address block (10 minutes)
Step 20. Seal the envelope flap (10 seconds)
Step 21. Consult a style guide for formal correspondence (15 minutes)
Step 22. Find the correct building name (5 minutes)
Step 23. Draft the body paragraphs (2 hours)
Step 24. Write your return address on the envelope (2 minutes)
Step 25. Affix the correct postage stamps (1 minute)
Step 26. Check the official's gender for proper pronouns (2 minutes)
Step 27. Print a copy of the letter for your personal records (2 minutes)
Step 28. Write the official's name on the envelope (1 minute)
Step 29. Select a professional font (5 minutes)
Step 30. Set the document margins to one inch (1 minute)
Step 31. Perform a final visual alignment check (2 minutes)
Step 32. Double-check the room number on the envelope (2 minutes)
Step 33. Ensure the date is correctly formatted (1 minute)
Step 34. Cite specific legislation or bill numbers (40 minutes)
Step 35. Prepare the enclosure list if sending attachments (10 minutes)
Step 36. Compose the concluding call to action (25 minutes)
Step 37. Confirm the official's current job title (15 minutes)
Step 38. Choose the appropriate closing (e.g., Sincerely) (5 minutes)
Step 39. Adjust the line spacing for readability (2 minutes)
Step 40. Open a new word processing document (30 seconds)
Step 41. Research the official's preferred method of contact (30 minutes)
Step 42. Verify the street address of the government office (15 minutes)
Step 43. Gather supporting data and statistics (3 hours)
Step 44. Clean the printer print-heads (10 minutes)
Step 45. Heat the wax for sealing (5 minutes)
Step 46. Select the paper size (Letter vs A4) (30 seconds)
Step 47. Write the first draft of the letter (1 hour)
Step 48. Check the current date (10 seconds)
Step 49. Review the address for any typos (5 minutes)
Step 50. Ensure the ink is dry before folding (3 minutes)
Step 51. Look up the official's website (5 minutes)
Step 52. Select a high-quality envelope (1 minute)
Step 53. Define the specific purpose of the letter (15 minutes)
Step 54. Edit the introduction for impact (15 minutes)
Step 55. List the key points to be covered (20 minutes)
Step 56. Analyze the official's recent voting record (1 hour)
Step 57. Identify the primary constituent concern (30 minutes)
Step 58. Find the official's public schedule for timing (20 minutes)
Step 59. Fold the letter into thirds (30 seconds)
Step 60. Reflect on the desired outcome of the letter (30 minutes)
Step 61. Fact-check the claims made in the body (45 minutes)
Step 62. Verify the official's current term status (10 minutes)
Step 63. Summarize the research findings (30 minutes)
Step 64. Add a postscript if necessary (5 minutes)
Step 65. Check the printer's ink levels (1 minute)
Step 66. Insert any additional brochures or flyers (2 minutes)
Step 67. Look up the proper protocol for addressing dignitaries (20 minutes)
Step 68. Determine the level of urgency (10 minutes)
Step 69. Proofread the signature line (1 minute)
Step 70. Perform a final read-through of the entire document (15 minutes)
Step 71. Take notes on the official's public statements (1 hour)
Step 72. Check for the most recent office relocation notices (15 minutes)
Step 73. Review the call to action for persuasiveness (20 minutes)
Step 74. Purchase professional stationery (1 hour)
Step 75. Verify the spelling of the city (2 minutes)
Step 76. Weigh the envelope for postage (2 minutes)
Step 77. Check the toner cartridge (2 minutes)
Step 78. Ensure the return address is legible (1 minute)
Step 79. File the record copy in a safe place (5 minutes)
Step 80. Verify the state abbreviation (1 minute)
Step 81. Double-check the recipient's name on the envelope (1 minute)
Step 82. Ensure the letter is centered on the page (2 minutes)
Step 83. Confirm the mailing district (5 minutes)
Step 84. Calibrate the printer settings (5 minutes)
Step 85. Check for any sensitive content (10 minutes)
Step 86. Verify your own phone number (1 minute)
Step 87. Write the delivery instructions (e.g., Personal) (1 minute)
Step 88. Search for the official's biography (15 minutes)
Step 89. Choose a professional font size (1 minute)
Step 90. Clear the workspace for assembly (5 minutes)
